from q2_table import where, order_by

def test_order_by_numeric():
    """Test order_by with numeric values"""
    rows = [
        {"name": "Alice", "age": "25", "city": "New York"},
        {"name": "Bob", "age": "30", "city": "London"},
        {"name": "Charlie", "age": "20", "city": "Paris"}
    ]
    result = order_by(rows, "age", False)
    assert len(result) == 3
    assert result[0]["name"] == "Charlie"  # age 20
    assert result[1]["name"] == "Alice"    # age 25
    assert result[2]["name"] == "Bob"      # age 30
    print("test_order_by_numeric passed")

def test_order_by_numeric_descending():
    """Test order_by with numeric values in descending order"""
    rows = [
        {"name": "Alice", "age": "25", "city": "New York"},
        {"name": "Bob", "age": "30", "city": "London"},
        {"name": "Charlie", "age": "20", "city": "Paris"}
    ]
    result = order_by(rows, "age", True)
    assert len(result) == 3
    assert result[0]["name"] == "Bob"      # age 30
    assert result[1]["name"] == "Alice"    # age 25
    assert result[2]["name"] == "Charlie"  # age 20
    print("test_order_by_numeric_descending passed")

def test_order_by_string():
    """Test order_by with string values"""
    rows = [
        {"name": "Alice", "age": "25", "city": "New York"},
        {"name": "Bob", "age": "30", "city": "London"},
        {"name": "Charlie", "age": "20", "city": "Paris"}
    ]
    result = order_by(rows, "city", False)
    assert len(result) == 3
    assert result[0]["name"] == "Bob"      # city "London"
    assert result[1]["name"] == "Alice"    # city "New York"
    assert result[2]["name"] == "Charlie"  # city "Paris"
    print("test_order_by_string passed")

def test_order_by_string_descending():
    """Test order_by with string values in descending order"""
    rows = [
        {"name": "Alice", "age": "25", "city": "New York"},
        {"name": "Bob", "age": "30", "city": "London"},
        {"name": "Charlie", "age": "20", "city": "Paris"}
    ]
    result = order_by(rows, "city", True)
    assert len(result) == 3
    assert result[0]["name"] == "Charlie"  # city "Paris"
    assert result[1]["name"] == "Alice"    # city "New York"
    assert result[2]["name"] == "Bob"      # city "London"
    print("test_order_by_string_descending passed")

def test_order_by_mixed_types():
    """Test order_by with mixed numeric and string values in column"""
    rows = [
        {"name": "Alice", "age": "25", "city": "New York"},
        {"name": "Bob", "age": "30", "city": "London"},
        {"name": "Charlie", "age": "20", "city": "Paris"}
    ]
    # Test with a column that has mixed types (should use string sorting)
    result = order_by(rows, "name", False)
    assert len(result) == 3
    assert result[0]["name"] == "Alice"    # name "Alice"
    assert result[1]["name"] == "Bob"      # name "Bob"
    assert result[2]["name"] == "Charlie"  # name "Charlie"
    print("test_order_by_mixed_types passed")

def test_order_by_empty_rows():
    """Test order_by with empty rows list"""
    result = order_by([], "age", False)
    assert result == []
    print("test_order_by_empty_rows passed")

def test_order_by_column_not_found():
    """Test order_by with non-existent column raises KeyError"""
    rows = [{"name": "Alice", "age": "25"}]
    try:
        order_by(rows, "city", False)
        assert False, "Should have raised KeyError"
    except KeyError:
        print("test_order_by_column_not_found passed")

def test_order_by_stable_sort():
    """Test that order_by maintains stable sort for equal values"""
    rows = [
        {"name": "Alice", "age": "25", "city": "New York"},
        {"name": "Bob", "age": "25", "city": "London"},
        {"name": "Charlie", "age": "25", "city": "Paris"}
    ]
    result = order_by(rows, "age", False)
    assert len(result) == 3
    # Should maintain original order for equal values
    assert result[0]["name"] == "Alice"
    assert result[1]["name"] == "Bob"
    assert result[2]["name"] == "Charlie"
    print("test_order_by_stable_sort passed")
